title: Sonda v2 scenario file
description: A synthetic-telemetry scenario for the sonda CLI and server. Accepts three top-level shapes: a canonical file with a `scenarios:` list, a single-signal shorthand with entry fields at the top level, or a `kind: composable` metric-pack definition.

AfterClause.description:
Structured after-clause expressing a causal dependency on another signal.

When present on a [`Entry`], the entry will not start emitting until the
referenced signal's latest value satisfies the comparison. Compilation of
after-clauses into runtime timing is handled in a later phase (PR 5).

# YAML example

```yaml
after:
  ref: cpu_signal
  op: ">"
  value: 90.0
  delay: "5s"
```

delay.description: Optional additional delay after the condition is met.

ref.description:
Target signal id to observe.

Serialized as `"ref"` in YAML because `ref` is a Rust keyword.

AfterOp.description:
Comparison operator for an [`AfterClause`] threshold check.

Serde maps `"<"` to [`LessThan`](AfterOp::LessThan) and `">"` to
[`GreaterThan`](AfterOp::GreaterThan). Any other value is rejected at
deserialization time.

oneOf.description: The referenced signal's value must be less than the threshold.
The referenced signal's value must be greater than the threshold.

AlertExpectation.description: One alert the scenario is expected to trigger.

alert.description:
Alert rule name — matched against the `alertname` label of the
`ALERTS` metric.

firing_within.description:
How long after scenario start the alert must reach `firing`
(e.g. `"2m"`).

labels.description: Additional label matchers the firing alert must carry.

resolves_within.description:
How long after scenario end the alert must stop firing. `None`
skips the resolution check.

BurstConfig.description:
Burst window configuration — a recurring high-rate period within a scenario.

During a burst the event rate is multiplied by `multiplier`. The burst
repeats on a fixed cycle defined by `every`, and each instance lasts for `for`.

If a gap and burst overlap in time, the gap takes priority and no events
are emitted.

for.description: How long each burst lasts (e.g. `"2s"`). Must be less than `every`.

multiplier.description: Rate multiplier during the burst (must be strictly positive).

CardinalitySpikeConfig.description:
Configuration for a cardinality spike — a recurring window that injects
dynamic label values to simulate cardinality explosions.

During the spike window, a label key is injected with one of `cardinality`
unique values per tick. Outside the window, the label key is absent.

# Example YAML

```yaml
cardinality_spikes:
  - label: pod_name
    every: 2m
    for: 30s
    cardinality: 500
    strategy: counter
    prefix: "pod-"
```

cardinality.description:
Number of unique label values generated during the spike.

Must be greater than zero.

for.description: How long each spike lasts (e.g. `"30s"`). Must be less than `every`.

label.description:
The label key to inject during the spike window.

Must be a valid Prometheus label key: `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.

prefix.description:
Optional prefix for generated label values.

Defaults to `"{label}_"` when not specified.

seed.description:
Optional RNG seed for the `random` strategy.

Ignored for the `counter` strategy.

strategy.description:
Strategy for generating unique label values.

Defaults to `counter` if not specified.

CsvColumnSpec.description:
Specification for a single CSV column in a multi-column `csv_replay`
configuration.

When the `columns` field is set on a `CsvReplay` generator config, each
`CsvColumnSpec` specifies a column index and the metric name to use when
that column is expanded into its own independent scenario.

# Example YAML

```yaml
columns:
  - index: 1
    name: cpu_percent
  - index: 2
    name: mem_percent
```

index.description: Zero-based column index in the CSV file.

labels.description:
Optional per-column labels merged with scenario-level labels during
expansion. Column labels override scenario-level labels on key conflict.

name.description: Metric name for the expanded scenario.

Defaults.description:
Shared defaults inherited by all entries in a v2 scenario file.

Fields set here act as fallbacks for entries that omit the corresponding
field. Defaults resolution is performed in a later compilation phase (PR 3),
not during parsing.

delay.description: Default `delay:` clause inherited by every entry.

duration.description:
Default total run duration (e.g. `"30s"`, `"5m"`). Applied per entry —
each entry runs for this long from its own resolved start, so a cascade's
total wall-clock is `max(phase_offset + duration)`, not `duration`.

labels.description: Default static labels merged into every entry.

on_sink_error.description: Default sink-error policy inherited by every entry.

rate.description: Default event rate in events per second.

start_time.description: Default emission-time anchor (absolute RFC 3339, signed offset, or `now`).

while.description: Default `while:` clause inherited by every entry.

DelayClause.description: Open/close debounce windows applied to a `while:` transition. Requires a `while:` clause on the same entry.

close.description: Debounce for the true → false transition. Either a duration string or an extended mapping.

oneOf.description: Duration shorthand, e.g. "5s".

open.description: Debounce for the false → true transition, e.g. "250ms", "5s".

Deviation.description:
One change an extension makes to a metric its base declares.

Modelled on YANG's `deviation`, and named for it: the base is never
edited, and stating a change is a different act from adding a metric.
Exactly one of `replace:` and `not_supported:` must be given.

# YAML Schema

```yaml
deviations:
  - metric: ifOperStatus
    replace:
      generator: { type: flap, up_value: 1.0, down_value: 2.0, period: 300s }
  - metric: ifHCOutOctets
    not_supported: true
```

metric.description:
Selector into the resolved base: `name`, or `name.id` where the base
repeats that name. Matching no spec is a hard error.

not_supported.description: Remove the addressed spec: this platform does not implement it.

replace.description: Fields to replace on the addressed spec.

DeviationReplace.description:
The fields a [`Deviation`] replaces, each wholesale.

A given `generator:` replaces the base's generator entirely and a given
`labels:` replaces the base's per-metric labels entirely. There is no
deep parameter merge: merging into a tagged generator enum has no
well-defined meaning, and a replacement that states its whole generator
is diffable. A field left out is inherited unchanged.

generator.description: Replacement generator for the addressed spec.

labels.description: Replacement per-metric labels for the addressed spec.

DistributionConfig.description:
Distribution model configuration for histogram and summary generators.

Determines how sample values are distributed when the generator produces
observations on each tick. Deserialized from YAML via the `type` tag.

# Example YAML

```yaml
distribution:
  type: exponential
  rate: 10.0
```

oneOf.description:
Exponential distribution with rate parameter lambda.

Mean = 1/lambda. Models latency distributions.

rate.description: Rate parameter (lambda). Must be strictly positive.

oneOf.description: Normal (Gaussian) distribution.

stddev.description: Spread of the distribution. Must be strictly positive.

oneOf.description: Uniform distribution over `[min, max]`.

DynamicLabelConfig.description:
Configuration for a dynamic label — an always-on rotating label value
attached to every emitted event.

Unlike [`CardinalitySpikeConfig`], dynamic labels are not time-windowed:
they appear in every event for the lifetime of the scenario. This enables
simulating a stable fleet of N distinct sources (e.g., 10 hostnames, 5 pod
names) without a spike/window concept.

# Example YAML (counter strategy)

```yaml
dynamic_labels:
  - key: hostname
    prefix: "host-"
    cardinality: 10
```

# Example YAML (values list strategy)

```yaml
dynamic_labels:
  - key: region
    values: [us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1]
```

key.description:
The label key to attach to every event.

Must be a valid Prometheus label key: `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.

anyOf.description:
Cycle through an explicit list of values.

The label value at each tick is `values[tick % values.len()]`.
Cardinality is implicit (length of the list).

values.description: The explicit list of label values to cycle through.

anyOf.description:
Sequential counter: `"{prefix}{tick % cardinality}"`.

Produces deterministic, predictable label values that cycle through
`cardinality` distinct values indefinitely.

cardinality.description: Number of unique label values in the cycle. Must be greater than zero.

prefix.description:
Prefix prepended to the counter index (e.g. `"host-"` produces
`"host-0"`, `"host-1"`, ...).

EncoderConfig.description:
Configuration selecting which encoder to use for a scenario.

This enum is serde-deserializable from YAML scenario files.
The `type` field selects the variant: `prometheus_text`, `influx_lp`,
`json_lines`, `syslog`, `remote_write`, or `otlp`.

Feature-gated encoders (`remote_write`, `otlp`) have companion
`*Disabled` variants that are compiled in when their feature is absent.
These accept the YAML tag so that deserialization succeeds with a
descriptive error from [`create_encoder`] instead of a generic
"unknown variant" error from serde.

oneOf.description:
Prometheus text exposition format (version 0.0.4).

`precision` optionally limits the number of decimal places in metric values.

precision.description: Maximum decimal places for metric values. `None` preserves full `f64` precision.

oneOf.description:
InfluxDB line protocol.

`field_key` sets the field key used for the metric value. Defaults to `"value"`.
`precision` optionally limits the number of decimal places in metric values.

field_key.description: The InfluxDB field key for the metric value. Defaults to `"value"` if absent.

precision.description: Maximum decimal places for metric values. `None` preserves full `f64` precision.

oneOf.description:
JSON Lines (NDJSON) format.

Each event is serialized as one JSON object per line. Compatible with Elasticsearch,
Loki, and generic HTTP ingest endpoints.

`precision` optionally rounds the metric value before JSON serialization.

precision.description: Maximum decimal places for metric values. `None` preserves full `f64` precision.

oneOf.description:
RFC 5424 syslog format.

Encodes log events as syslog lines. `hostname` and `app_name` default to `"sonda"`.

app_name.description: The APP-NAME field in the syslog header. Defaults to `"sonda"`.

hostname.description: The HOSTNAME field in the syslog header. Defaults to `"sonda"`.

oneOf.description:
Prometheus remote write protobuf format.

Encodes metric events as length-prefixed protobuf `TimeSeries` messages.
Must be paired with the `remote_write` sink type, which batches TimeSeries
into a single `WriteRequest`, snappy-compresses, and HTTP POSTs with the
correct protocol headers. Requires the `remote-write` feature flag.

OTLP protobuf format.

Encodes metric events as length-prefixed protobuf `Metric` messages and
log events as length-prefixed protobuf `LogRecord` messages. Must be
paired with the `otlp_grpc` sink type, which batches and sends via gRPC.
Requires the `otlp` feature flag.

Entry.description:
A single scenario entry in a v2 file.

An entry is either an **inline signal** (has `generator` and `name`) or a
**pack reference** (has `pack`). The two forms are mutually exclusive,
enforced at parse time.

All fields are optional in the struct to support flexible YAML authoring.
Semantic validation (required fields, mutual exclusion) is performed by
[`parse::parse`].

after.description: Causal dependency on another signal's value.

clock_group.description: Clock group for coordinated timing across entries.

delay.description: Open / close debounce windows applied to `while_clause` transitions.

distribution.description: Distribution model for histogram or summary observations.

gap_windows.description: One-shot silent windows at fixed offsets from scenario start.

id.description: Unique identifier for causal dependency references (`after.ref`).

jitter.description: Jitter amplitude applied to generated values.

labels.description: Static labels attached to every emitted event.

log_generator.description:
Log generator configuration (for logs signal type).

Mutually exclusive with `generator` — an entry uses one or the other
depending on `signal_type`.

mean_shift_per_sec.description: Linear drift applied to the distribution mean each second.

name.description: Metric or scenario name. Required for inline entries.

observations_per_tick.description: Number of observations sampled per tick.

overrides.description: Per-metric overrides within the referenced pack.

pack.description: Pack name or file path. Mutually exclusive with `generator`.

phase_offset.description: Phase offset for staggered start within a clock group.

rate.description: Event rate in events per second.

start_time.description: Emission-time anchor (absolute RFC 3339, signed offset, or `now`).

while.description: Continuous lifecycle gate on another signal's value.

ExpectConfig.description: Top-level `expect:` block of a scenario file.

alerts.description: Alert expectations, checked in order. Must not be empty.

FlapEnum.description:
Domain-specific value mapping for the [`GeneratorConfig::Flap`] alias.

The variant selects an `(up_value, down_value)` pair aligned with
gNMI / openconfig conventions:

| Variant | `up_value` | `down_value` | Convention |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Boolean` | 1.0 | 0.0 | Generic boolean |
| `LinkState` | 1.0 | 0.0 | Synonym of `Boolean` |
| `OperState` | 1.0 | 2.0 | gNMI oper-state (UP=1, DOWN=2) |
| `AdminState` | 1.0 | 2.0 | gNMI admin-state (UP=1, DOWN=2) |
| `NeighborState` | 6.0 | 1.0 | BGP neighbor-state (ESTABLISHED=6, IDLE=1) |

FlatFile.description:
A flat representation of a single-entry v2 file (no `scenarios:` key).

This is an internal deserialization target used to support the shorthand
format where the top-level YAML mapping contains entry fields directly.

GapConfig.description:
Gap window configuration — a recurring silent period within a scenario.

During a gap the scheduler emits no events. The gap repeats on a fixed
cycle defined by `every`, and each instance lasts for `for`.

for.description: How long each gap lasts (e.g. `"20s"`). Must be less than `every`.

GapWindowConfig.description:
One non-recurring silent window at a known offset from scenario start.

The sibling of [`GapConfig`] for silence that *happened* rather than
silence that *recurs*. A periodic gap answers "simulate a scrape gap every
60s"; this answers "the exporter was down from 04:12 to 04:19", which has
no period to speak of.

It is a separate field rather than a new shape on `gaps:` deliberately: an
untagged enum on an existing public config key risks silently
reinterpreting YAML that already parses, and a sibling field is additive
and boring.

at.description:
Offset from scenario start at which the silence begins (e.g. `"60s"`).

An offset, not a length: `"0s"` is a scenario that begins already
inside the silence, which is what a capture taken during an outage
looks like.

GeneratorConfig.description:
Configuration for a value generator, used for YAML deserialization.

The `type` field selects which generator to instantiate. Additional fields
are specific to each variant.

# Core generators

```yaml
generator:
  type: sine
  amplitude: 5.0
  period_secs: 30
  offset: 10.0
```

# Operational aliases

Aliases desugar into core generators at config expansion time. They use
domain-relevant parameter names and have sensible defaults.

```yaml
# Normal healthy oscillation (desugars to sine + jitter)
generator:
  type: steady
  center: 75.0
  amplitude: 10.0
  period: "60s"
  noise: 2.0

# Resource leak (desugars to sawtooth)
generator:
  type: leak
  baseline: 40.0
  ceiling: 95.0
  time_to_ceiling: "120s"

# Interface flap (desugars to sequence)
generator:
  type: flap
  up_duration: "10s"
  down_duration: "5s"
```

oneOf.description: A generator that always returns the same value.

value.description: The fixed value returned on every tick.

oneOf.description: A generator that returns deterministically random values in `[min, max]`.

max.description: Upper bound of the output range (inclusive).

min.description: Lower bound of the output range (inclusive).

seed.description: Optional seed for deterministic replay. Defaults to 0 when absent.

oneOf.description: A generator that follows a sine curve.

amplitude.description: Half the peak-to-peak swing of the wave.

offset.description: Vertical offset applied to every sample (the wave's midpoint).

period_secs.description: Duration of one full cycle in seconds.

oneOf.description: A generator that linearly ramps from `min` to `max` then resets.

max.description: Value approached at the end of each period (never reached).

min.description: Value at the start of each period.

period_secs.description: Duration of one full ramp in seconds.

oneOf.description: A generator that steps through an explicit sequence of values.

repeat.description:
When true (default), the sequence cycles. When false, the last value
is returned for all ticks beyond the sequence length.

values.description: The ordered list of values to step through. Must not be empty.

oneOf.description: A generator that outputs a baseline value with periodic spikes.

baseline.description: The normal output value between spikes.

duration_secs.description: How long each spike lasts in seconds.

interval_secs.description: Time between spike starts in seconds.

magnitude.description: The amount added to baseline during a spike.

oneOf.description: A generator that replays numeric values from a CSV file.

columns.description:
Explicit column specifications. When present, the config layer
expands this single scenario into N independent single-column
scenarios before launch.

When absent, columns are auto-discovered from the CSV header row.
An empty list is an error.

default_metric_name.description:
Fallback metric name for auto-discovered columns whose header has
no `__name__`. Suffixed with `_<index>` when multiple such columns
share the fallback.

file.description: Path to the CSV file containing numeric values.

repeat.description:
Whether to loop back to the first value after exhausting the CSV.
Defaults to `true`.

timescale.description:
Replay speed multiplier (default `1.0`). `2.0` plays 2× faster,
`0.5` plays 2× slower. Must be strictly positive.

oneOf.description:
A monotonic step counter: `start + tick * step_size`, with optional wrap-around.

Useful for testing `rate()` and `increase()` PromQL functions.

max.description:
Optional wrap-around threshold. When set and greater than `start`,
the value wraps via modular arithmetic.

start.description: Initial value at tick 0. Defaults to 0.0 when absent.

oneOf.description:
Binary up/down toggle modeling an interface flap.

Desugars into a [`Sequence`](GeneratorConfig::Sequence) generator that
alternates between `up_value` (default 1.0) and `down_value` (default 0.0).
The number of consecutive up/down ticks is derived from `up_duration` and
`down_duration` relative to the scenario `rate`.

The optional `enum:` shorthand selects up/down values aligned with
common gNMI / openconfig conventions (oper-state, admin-state,
BGP neighbor-state). Mutually exclusive with explicit `up_value` /
`down_value`.

# Example YAML

```yaml
generator:
  type: flap
  up_duration: "10s"
  down_duration: "5s"
  enum: oper_state    # up_value=1.0, down_value=2.0
```

down_duration.description:
How long the signal stays in the "down" state per cycle.
Defaults to `"5s"`.

down_value.description: Value emitted during the "down" state. Defaults to `0.0`.

enum.description:
Domain-specific shorthand selecting `(up_value, down_value)` per
the [`FlapEnum`] mapping. Mutually exclusive with `up_value` /
`down_value`.

up_duration.description:
How long the signal stays in the "up" state per cycle.
Defaults to `"10s"`.

up_value.description: Value emitted during the "up" state. Defaults to `1.0`.

oneOf.description:
Resource filling up and resetting on a repeating cycle (e.g. disk usage
sawtoothing after log rotation).

Desugars into a [`Sawtooth`](GeneratorConfig::Sawtooth) generator with
`min = baseline`, `max = ceiling`, `period_secs` derived from
`time_to_saturate`. The sawtooth resets to `baseline` after each
`time_to_saturate` period, modeling a resource that fills and is
periodically reclaimed.

# Distinction from `Leak`

- **Saturation**: repeating fill-and-reset cycle. Default period is
  `"5m"`.
- **Leak**: one-way ramp, no reset expected within the scenario
  duration. Default period is `"10m"`.

# Example YAML

```yaml
generator:
  type: saturation
  baseline: 20.0
  ceiling: 95.0
  time_to_saturate: "5m"
```

baseline.description: Resource level at the start of each cycle. Defaults to `0.0`.

ceiling.description: Maximum resource level before reset. Defaults to `100.0`.

time_to_saturate.description: Duration of one fill cycle. Defaults to `"5m"`.

oneOf.description:
Resource growing toward a ceiling without resetting — a one-way ramp
modeling a memory leak or similar resource exhaustion.

Desugars into a [`Sawtooth`](GeneratorConfig::Sawtooth) generator.
The intent is that `time_to_ceiling` equals or exceeds the scenario
`duration` so values only ramp upward and never reset within the run.
If the scenario has a `duration` set and `time_to_ceiling` is shorter
than that duration, desugaring returns a config error because the
sawtooth would reset mid-run, which is the
[`Saturation`](GeneratorConfig::Saturation) pattern instead.

# Distinction from `Saturation`

- **Leak**: one-way ramp, no reset expected. `time_to_ceiling` should
  be >= scenario `duration`. Default period is `"10m"`.
- **Saturation**: repeating fill-and-reset cycle. Default period is
  `"5m"`.

# Example YAML

```yaml
generator:
  type: leak
  baseline: 40.0
  ceiling: 95.0
  time_to_ceiling: "120s"
```

time_to_ceiling.description:
Time to grow from baseline to ceiling. Defaults to `"10m"`.
The sawtooth period is set to this value so values only ramp
upward within the scenario duration.

oneOf.description:
Gradual performance loss with noise — models degradation over time
(e.g. growing latency, increasing error rate).

Desugars into a [`Sawtooth`](GeneratorConfig::Sawtooth) generator with
jitter automatically applied on [`BaseScheduleConfig`].

# Example YAML

```yaml
generator:
  type: degradation
  baseline: 0.05
  ceiling: 0.5
  time_to_degrade: "60s"
  noise: 0.02
```

noise.description: Jitter amplitude added as noise. Defaults to `1.0`.

noise_seed.description: Seed for the noise generator. Defaults to `0`.

time_to_degrade.description: Duration of the degradation ramp. Defaults to `"5m"`.

oneOf.description:
Normal healthy oscillation around a center value — the "everything is
fine" baseline signal.

Desugars into a [`Sine`](GeneratorConfig::Sine) generator with jitter
automatically applied on [`BaseScheduleConfig`].

# Example YAML

```yaml
generator:
  type: steady
  center: 75.0
  amplitude: 10.0
  period: "60s"
  noise: 2.0
```

amplitude.description: Half the peak-to-peak swing. Defaults to `10.0`.

center.description: Center of the oscillation (the sine wave's offset). Defaults to `50.0`.

noise.description: Jitter amplitude added as noise. Defaults to `1.0`.

noise_seed.description: Seed for the noise generator. Defaults to `0`.

period.description: Duration of one full oscillation cycle. Defaults to `"60s"`.

oneOf.description:
Periodic anomalous bursts above a baseline — models sudden spikes
in CPU, memory, or request rate.

Desugars into a [`Spike`](GeneratorConfig::Spike) generator.

# Example YAML

```yaml
generator:
  type: spike_event
  baseline: 35.0
  spike_height: 60.0
  spike_duration: "10s"
  spike_interval: "30s"
```

baseline.description: Normal output value between spikes. Defaults to `0.0`.

spike_duration.description: How long each spike lasts. Defaults to `"10s"`.

spike_height.description: Amount added to baseline during a spike. Defaults to `100.0`.

spike_interval.description: Time between spike starts. Defaults to `"30s"`.

KafkaSaslConfig.description:
SASL authentication configuration for Kafka broker connections.

Supported mechanisms are `PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256`, and `SCRAM-SHA-512`.

KafkaTlsConfig.description:
TLS configuration for Kafka broker connections.

When `enabled` is `true`, the Kafka sink connects to brokers over TLS.
An optional `ca_cert` path can be provided to trust a custom or self-signed
CA certificate. When `ca_cert` is omitted, Mozilla's bundled root
certificates are used via [`webpki_roots`].

ca_cert.description:
Optional path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate file for custom or
self-signed CAs. When omitted, Mozilla's bundled root certificates are used.

enabled.description: Enable TLS for broker connections. Default: `false`.

Kind.description:
Discriminator declaring the role of a v2 YAML file.

Required at the top level of every v2 scenario file. `Runnable` files
carry one or more scenario entries (inline or via `pack:` references)
and are executable. `Composable` files are pack definitions; their
body matches [`MetricPackDef`](crate::packs::MetricPackDef) and they
are referenced from runnable files via `pack:`.

LogCsvColumns.description:
Column-role assignment for a [`LogCsvReplayGenerator`].

`timestamp`, `severity`, and `message` map header column names to their
semantic role. Any header column not referenced here becomes a free-form
`fields` entry on the emitted [`LogEvent`].

LogGeneratorConfig.description:
Configuration for a log generator, used for YAML deserialization.

The `type` field selects which generator to instantiate.

# Example YAML — template generator

```yaml
generator:
  type: template
  templates:
    - message: "Request from {ip} to {endpoint}"
      field_pools:
        ip: ["10.0.0.1", "10.0.0.2"]
        endpoint: ["/api", "/health"]
  severity_weights:
    info: 0.7
    warn: 0.2
    error: 0.1
  seed: 42
```

# Example YAML — csv_replay generator

```yaml
generator:
  type: csv_replay
  file: logs.csv
  timescale: 1.0
  default_severity: info
  repeat: true
  columns:
    timestamp: timestamp
    severity: severity
    message: message
```

oneOf.description: Generates events from message templates with randomized field pool values.

seed.description: Seed for deterministic replay. Defaults to `0` when absent.

severity_weights.description:
Optional severity weight map. Keys are severity names (`info`, `warn`, etc.),
values are relative weights. Defaults to `info: 1.0` when absent.

templates.description: One or more template entries. Templates are selected round-robin by tick.

oneOf.description:
Replays structured log events from a CSV file with `timestamp`,
`severity`, `message`, and arbitrary field columns.

The scenario rate is derived from the median Δt of the timestamp
column at config-expansion time; a user-supplied `rate:` is always
overridden (a `tracing::warn!` records the override).

columns.description:
Optional explicit column-role mapping. When absent, roles are
auto-discovered from the CSV header.

default_severity.description:
Fallback severity when the severity cell is missing or unparseable.
Defaults to `Info`.

repeat.description: Whether to cycle rows after exhausting the CSV. Defaults to `true`.

timescale.description: Replay speed multiplier (default `1.0`, must be strictly positive).

MetricOverride.description:
Per-metric override within a [`PackScenarioConfig`] or a v2 pack-backed
scenario entry.

Allows the user to customize the generator, add extra labels, or attach a
causal dependency (`after:`) for a specific metric without modifying the
pack definition. The v1 expansion path ([`expand_pack`]) consumes only
`generator` and `labels`; the v2 compiler additionally propagates `after`
onto the expanded signal (see
[`crate::compiler::expand`]).

after.description:
Optional causal dependency (`after:`) attached specifically to this
expanded metric.

Per spec §2.4, a per-metric `after:` on a pack override sets a
causal dependency for that specific expanded signal, overriding
any entry-level `after` on the parent pack entry. The v2 compiler
propagates this onto the resulting signal in Phase 3; v1 pack
expansion ignores the field.

delay.description:
Per-metric `delay:` clause; replaces any entry-level `delay:` for
this expanded signal.

labels.description:
Additional labels merged on top of all other label sources.

Uses `BTreeMap` for deterministic serialization order, consistent with
the v2 AST label types.

while.description:
Per-metric `while:` clause; replaces any entry-level `while:` for
this expanded signal.

MetricPackDef.description:
A metric pack definition: a reusable bundle of metric names and label schemas.

Packs are templates — they contain no rate, duration, sink, or encoder.
Those come from the user via [`PackScenarioConfig`] at expansion time.

# YAML Schema

```yaml
name: telegraf_snmp_interface
description: "Standard SNMP interface metrics (Telegraf-normalized)"
category: network
shared_labels:
  device: ""
  job: snmp
metrics:
  - name: ifOperStatus
    generator:
      type: constant
      value: 1.0
  - name: ifHCInOctets
    generator:
      type: step
      step_size: 125000.0
```

A pack may instead extend another, adding metrics and deviating from the
base's — see [`extends`](Self::extends) and [`extend`](crate::packs::extend).

deviations.description: Changes to the base's metrics. Meaningful only with `extends:`.

extends.description:
The pack this one extends, by the same reference form `pack:` accepts.

One value, not a list: multiple inheritance would need a diamond merge
order, and an extension of two bases is two packs. Chains are allowed
and unbounded. Resolved through the same resolver chain as `pack:`, so
an extension extends the *resolved* base — shadow the base in
`--catalog <dir>` and every extension built on it inherits the shadow.

metrics.description:
The metric specifications this pack contributes.

In an extension these are **purely additive**: a spec whose selector
the base already declares is a hard error, because adding and
changing are different operations. Use a [`Deviation`] to change one.

Empty is legal only for an extension — a pack that resolves to no
metrics at all is [`ExpandError::EmptyPack`](crate::compiler::expand::ExpandError).

shared_labels.description:
Labels shared across all metrics in the pack. Per-metric labels and
user labels are merged on top (user wins on conflict).

An extension's map is merged over its base's, so the extension wins
and deeper packs win in chain order.

MetricSpec.description:
A single metric within a pack definition.

Specifies the metric name and optionally per-metric labels and a default
generator. When the generator is absent, [`expand_pack`] uses a
`constant { value: 0.0 }` default.

generator.description:
Default value generator for this metric. When absent, a constant(0.0)
generator is used.

id.description:
Disambiguator among specs sharing a [`name`](Self::name), and the
second half of this spec's selector.

Required — and unique — on every member of a repeated name; optional
when the name occurs once. It stands for what the repetition is *by*:
the CPU mode, the memory field, the SNMP column.

labels.description: Labels specific to this metric, merged on top of the pack's shared labels.

name.description:
The metric name (e.g. `"ifHCInOctets"`, `"node_cpu_seconds_total"`).

May not contain `.` — that is the selector separator, and
[`validate_pack`] enforces the exclusion so `name.id` can never be
ambushed by a dotted name.

OnSinkError.description:
Policy for handling sink I/O errors during a running scenario.

`Warn` (the default) logs a rate-limited message, increments error stats,
drops the failing batch, and continues ticking. `Fail` propagates the
error and terminates the scenario thread — the historical behavior.

OtlpSignalType.description:
Selects which OTLP signal type the sink handles.

Determines both the gRPC path and the parsing/batching strategy.

oneOf.description:
Metric signal — data is parsed as OTLP `Metric` messages and sent
to the `MetricsService/Export` gRPC endpoint.

Log signal — data is parsed as OTLP `LogRecord` messages and sent
to the `LogsService/Export` gRPC endpoint.

PromMetricType.description: Prometheus exposition metric kind for `# TYPE` annotations.

RetryConfig.description:
Serde-deserializable retry configuration embedded in sink YAML blocks.

All three fields are required when the `retry:` block is present.

# Example YAML

```yaml
retry:
  max_attempts: 3
  initial_backoff: 100ms
  max_backoff: 5s
```

initial_backoff.description:
Duration string for the first retry delay (e.g. `"100ms"`, `"1s"`).

Parsed by [`parse_duration`](crate::config::validate::parse_duration).

max_attempts.description:
Number of retry attempts after the initial failure.

The total number of calls is `max_attempts + 1` (one initial attempt
plus up to `max_attempts` retries). Must be at least 1.

max_backoff.description:
Duration string for the maximum backoff cap (e.g. `"5s"`, `"30s"`).

Must be greater than or equal to `initial_backoff`. Parsed by
[`parse_duration`](crate::config::validate::parse_duration).

ScenarioFileCanonical.description:
A parsed v2 scenario file.

This is the top-level AST node produced by [`parse::parse`]. It captures
the exact structure of the YAML input without resolving defaults, expanding
packs, or compiling after-clauses.

# Catalog metadata

The three optional fields [`scenario_name`](Self::scenario_name),
[`category`](Self::category), and [`description`](Self::description)
carry top-level metadata used by catalog probes. The compiler pipeline
itself (normalize → expand → compile_after → prepare) does **not** consume
these fields — they are pure metadata, not compile input.

category.description:
Legacy catalog category. Superseded by `tags` (filtered via
`sonda list --tag`). Carried through for back-compat with files
authored before 1.9a; not surfaced by the current CLI.

defaults.description: Optional shared defaults inherited by all entries.

description.description:
One-line human-readable description surfaced by `sonda list` and
`sonda show`. Pure metadata — ignored by every compiler phase.

expect.description:
Optional alert expectations consumed by `sonda test`. Pure metadata —
ignored by every compiler phase and by the runtime.

kind.description:
Discriminator declaring whether the file is a runnable scenario
or a composable pack definition.

scenario_name.description:
Catalog display name (kebab-case). When present it overrides the
filename-derived name in the CLI catalog probe. Pure metadata —
ignored by every compiler phase.

scenarios.description:
One or more scenario entries (inline signals or pack references).
Empty when `kind: composable` — composable files carry no entries.

tags.description:
Optional file-level metadata tags surfaced by `sonda list --tag`.
Carried through normalization unchanged; ignored at runtime.

Severity.description:
The severity level of a log event.

Variants map to the conventional log severity ladder. Serializes to and from
lowercase strings (e.g., `"info"`, `"error"`) for YAML and JSON compatibility.

oneOf.description: Extremely detailed diagnostic information.
Diagnostic information useful during development.
General informational messages.
Potentially harmful situations that warrant attention.
Error events that may allow the application to continue.
Severe error events that will likely cause the application to abort.

SinkConfig.description:
Configuration selecting which sink to use for a scenario.

This enum is serde-deserializable from YAML scenario files.
The `type` field selects the variant: `stdout`, `file`, `tcp`, `udp`,
`http_push`, `remote_write`, `kafka`, `loki`, or `otlp_grpc`.

Feature-gated sinks (`http_push`, `loki`, `remote_write`, `kafka`,
`otlp_grpc`) have companion `*Disabled` variants that are compiled in
when their feature is absent. These accept the YAML tag so that
deserialization succeeds with a descriptive error from [`create_sink`]
instead of a generic "unknown variant" error from serde.

oneOf.description: Write encoded events to stdout, buffered via [`BufWriter`](std::io::BufWriter).

Write encoded events to a file at the given path.

Parent directories are created automatically if they do not exist.

path.description: Filesystem path to write encoded events to.

oneOf.description:
Write encoded events over a persistent TCP connection.

The sink connects on construction and buffers writes via [`BufWriter`](std::io::BufWriter).

address.description: Remote address to connect to, e.g. `"127.0.0.1:9999"`.

retry.description: Optional retry policy for transient failures.

oneOf.description:
Send each encoded event as a single UDP datagram.

No connection is established; an ephemeral local port is bound and each
call to `write` sends one `send_to` datagram.

address.description: Remote address to send datagrams to, e.g. `"127.0.0.1:9999"`.

oneOf.description:
In-process memory sink for tests and benchmarks.

When `capture` is `true`, each write records its `Instant` alongside
the bytes, bounded to the most recent `max_events` entries. When
`capture` is `false`, the sink only accumulates bytes in its buffer.
Programmatic embedders can pass `capture_handle: Some(arc)` to mirror
writes into an externally-owned ring; YAML scenarios always leave it
`None` because the field is `serde(skip)`.

capture.description: Whether to record `(Instant, bytes)` on every write.

max_events.description:
Cap on retained captured events. Defaults to `1_000_000` when
`capture` is `true` and the field is omitted.

oneOf.description:
Batch encoded events and deliver them via HTTP POST.

Bytes are accumulated in a buffer until `batch_size` bytes are reached,
then flushed as a single POST request. The `flush()` method sends any
remaining buffered data.

Requires the `http` Cargo feature to be enabled.

batch_size.description: Optional flush threshold in bytes. Defaults to 4 KiB if not specified.

content_type.description:
Optional `Content-Type` header value. Defaults to
`"application/octet-stream"` if not specified.

headers.description:
Optional extra HTTP headers to send with every POST request.

When provided, these headers are sent in addition to the `Content-Type`
header. Useful for protocols that require specific headers, such as
Prometheus remote write (`Content-Encoding: snappy`,
`X-Prometheus-Remote-Write-Version: 0.1.0`).

max_buffer_age.description:
Maximum batch age before a time-based flush, e.g. `"5s"`. Defaults
to `"5s"`; a zero value (e.g. `"0s"`) disables time-based flushing.

retry.description:
Optional retry policy for transient failures.

When absent, the sink fails immediately on errors (no retry).

url.description: Target URL for HTTP POST requests, e.g. `"http://localhost:9090/api/v1/write"`.

oneOf.description:
Batch TimeSeries and deliver them as Prometheus remote write requests.

This sink is designed to be paired with the `remote_write` encoder, which
produces length-prefixed protobuf `TimeSeries` bytes. The sink accumulates
TimeSeries entries and, on flush or when `batch_size` is reached, wraps them
in a single `WriteRequest`, prost-encodes, snappy-compresses, and HTTP POSTs
with the correct remote write protocol headers.

Requires the `remote-write` Cargo feature to be enabled.

batch_size.description:
Flush threshold in number of TimeSeries entries. Defaults to 100 if
not specified.

max_buffer_age.description:
Maximum batch age before a time-based flush, e.g. `"5s"`. Defaults
to `"5s"`; a zero value (e.g. `"0s"`) disables time-based flushing.

retry.description: Optional retry policy for transient failures.

url.description:
Target URL for the remote write endpoint, e.g.
`"http://localhost:8428/api/v1/write"`.

oneOf.description:
Batch encoded events and deliver them to a Kafka topic.

Uses [`rskafka`](https://crates.io/crates/rskafka) — a pure-Rust Kafka
client with no C dependencies — for musl-compatible static linking.

Bytes are accumulated in an internal buffer. When the buffer reaches
64 KiB, or when `flush()` is called explicitly, the buffer is published
as a single Kafka record to partition 0 of the configured topic.

Requires the `kafka` Cargo feature to be enabled.

brokers.description:
Comma-separated list of broker `host:port` addresses,
e.g. `"127.0.0.1:9092"` or `"broker1:9092,broker2:9092"`.

max_buffer_age.description:
Maximum batch age before a time-based flush, e.g. `"5s"`. Defaults
to `"5s"`; a zero value (e.g. `"0s"`) disables time-based flushing.

retry.description: Optional retry policy for transient failures.

tls.description: Optional TLS configuration for encrypted broker connections.

topic.description: The Kafka topic name to produce records to.

oneOf.description:
Batch encoded log lines and deliver them to Grafana Loki via HTTP POST.
Entries are grouped by combined label set (constructor labels + per-event
overlay from `dynamic_labels`) into one stream per unique combination.
Requires the `http` Cargo feature.

max_buffer_age.description:
Maximum batch age before a time-based flush, e.g. `"5s"`. Defaults
to `"5s"`; a zero value (e.g. `"0s"`) disables time-based flushing.

max_streams_per_push.description:
Hard cap on unique streams per push. Defaults to
[`DEFAULT_MAX_STREAMS_PER_PUSH`](loki::DEFAULT_MAX_STREAMS_PER_PUSH).

retry.description: Optional retry policy for transient failures.

url.description: Base URL of the Loki instance, e.g. `"http://localhost:3100"`.

oneOf.description:
Batch OTLP protobuf data and deliver via gRPC to an OpenTelemetry Collector.

This sink is designed to be paired with the `otlp` encoder, which produces
length-prefixed protobuf `Metric` or `LogRecord` bytes. The sink accumulates
entries and, on flush or when `batch_size` is reached, wraps them in the
appropriate OTLP export request and sends via gRPC.

Requires the `otlp` Cargo feature to be enabled.

batch_size.description:
Flush threshold in number of data points / log records.
Defaults to 100 if not specified.

max_buffer_age.description:
Maximum batch age before a time-based flush, e.g. `"5s"`. Defaults
to `"5s"`; a zero value (e.g. `"0s"`) disables time-based flushing.

retry.description: Optional retry policy for transient failures.

signal_type.description: Whether to send metrics or logs.

SpikeStrategy.description:
Strategy for generating unique label values during a cardinality spike.

Determines how the spike window produces distinct values for the injected
label key on each tick.

oneOf.description:
Sequential counter: `prefix + (tick % cardinality)`.

Produces deterministic, predictable label values without needing a seed.

Deterministic random: SplitMix64 hash of `seed ^ tick`, formatted as hex.

Produces label values that look random but are reproducible given the
same seed.

TemplateConfig.description:
Configuration for one message template used by [`LogGeneratorConfig::Template`].

The `message` field may contain `{placeholder}` tokens that are resolved
using the corresponding value pool from `field_pools`.

# Example YAML

```yaml
message: "Request from {ip} to {endpoint}"
field_pools:
  ip:
    - "10.0.0.1"
    - "10.0.0.2"
  endpoint:
    - "/api"
    - "/health"
```

field_pools.description:
Maps placeholder names to their value pools.

Uses `BTreeMap` for deterministic iteration order, matching the
codebase convention for ordered maps.

message.description: The message template. Use `{field_name}` for dynamic placeholders.

UnresolvedBehavior.description:
Policy applied when a cross-POST `while:` reference cannot be resolved at
scenario start. Only meaningful when [`WhileClause::scenario_name`] is set.

oneOf.description: Treat the gate as open until the upstream registers.
Treat the gate as closed until the upstream registers.
Hold the scenario in `unresolved` state until the upstream registers.

WhileClause.description:
Continuous lifecycle gate on another signal's value.

```yaml
while:
  ref: link_state
  op: ">"
  value: 0
```

WhileOp.description:
Strict comparison operator for a [`WhileClause`].

Only `<` and `>` are accepted. Non-strict operators (`<=`, `>=`, `==`,
`!=`) are rejected at deserialize time with a hint pointing to the
strict alternatives — equality on `f64` over a continuous gate is
numerically unsafe and forbidden by design.
